subject: Pioneer Analytics MAP: performance scope & acceptance (latency/TTFT/concurrency)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneer.ai>, Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pioneer MAP: performance scope & acceptance (latency/TTFT/concurrency)

Hi Liam / Sarah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great conversation. Per our MAP, attached is the proposed performance benchmarking plan we'll run as part of the evaluation window. The goal is to validate production economics and service-levels for your primary inference workload so we can finalize the pilot close timeline. Attachment: Pioneer_MAP_Benchmark_Plan_v1.xlsx (plan + workload definitions).

Key points (high level):
- Evaluation window: 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-09 (2-day scheduled run; we can shift if you need).
- Workload mix: 60% short prompts ( <= 64 tokens ), 30% medium (65-512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens). We will replay a sample set you provide and supplement with synthetic traffic to reach steady-state.
- Throughput targets: steady-state 50 QPS sustained, peak bursts to 200 QPS for 2-minute windows to emulate traffic spikes.
- Concurrency target: 200 concurrent requests (aligned with peak burst).
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) SLOs: p50 < 120 ms, p90 < 220 ms, p99 < 350 ms (measured at the server egress of the first token; we will include client-sided measurement for cross-check).
- Per-token latency (subsequent tokens): p50/p90/p99 targets in plan (see sheet 'SLOs').
- Success criteria: pass if all critical SLOs met and no more than 2% request error rate for the run.

Asks for you to confirm so we scope correctly:
1) Can you share the sanitized prompt corpus (CSV) and expected tokenization (model + tokenizer) by EOD 2026-10-06?
2) Which environment should we target first: hosted Redwood API or your dedicated/private pilot environment? (We prefer hosted for faster iteration; dedicated is fine if you require isolated data handling.)
3) Any additional latency constraints from sidecars/proxies we should instrument for (CDN, edge sidecars)?

Operational notes:
- We'll run each scenario 3x and report median + variance.
- We will provide a runbook and raw CSV results + Grafana snapshots after the run.
- Attachments in the run will be lightweight (CSV results + screenshots).

Proposed timeline:
- 10/06: finalize corpus + endpoint details
- 10/08–10/09: benchmarking runs
- 10/09–10/12: results analysis + enablement call
- 10/12: MAP acceptance and next-step (canary/rollout) decision

If that sounds good I'll schedule the run and loop in Neha (performance lead) to coordinate test harness and experiments.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Pioneer_MAP_Benchmark_Plan_v1.xlsx (workload sheets, SLOs, run sequence)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneer.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@pioneer.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pioneer MAP: performance scope & acceptance (latency/TTFT/concurrency)

Hi Olga — thanks for the plan and quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions before we lock the corpus and run window: 

1) TTFT measurement: can you confirm the measurement point? You state 'server egress of the first token' — we typically measure TTFT from our client SDK (seen by end-user). We'll want both, but for acceptance we need the client-observed TTFT to be under 250 ms p99. Can you include a client-side sim?

2) Load profile: our production peaks are closer to 120 QPS steady with 350 QPS spikes for <30s. Can you cover a configuration to exercise that peak (we want to see failure modes above 200 QPS)?

3) Dataset: attaching a sanitized sample prompt set (pioneer-sample-1000.jsonl). It includes a mix of prompts and expected token lengths.

4) Security: we'll need the run artifacts stored in our S3 bucket and a signed access ACL. Also, SOC2 evidence was requested by procurement; can you attach the SOC2 section for logging and retention?

If you can confirm the measurement points and add an additional peak profile (350 QPS spike), we can finalize and get you the full corpus by EOD 10/06.

Appreciate it — Liam
Director, Platform Engineering
Pioneer Analytics

--
Attachment: pioneer-sample-1000.jsonl (sanitized prompts)

Date: 2026-10-07T08:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Pioneer MAP: performance scope & acceptance (latency/TTFT/concurrency)

Neha — forwarding Liam's reply. TL;DR: they want client-observed TTFT p99 <= 250ms (for acceptance) and an extra peak profile: 350 QPS spikes (short duration). Also storage of artifacts into their S3 and SOC2 evidence.

Can you own the run config and the extra spike test? Specific tasks: 
- Add a second peak profile to the plan: 120 QPS steady, 350 QPS spikes of 30s (3 times)
- Ensure our harness reports both server-side and simulated client-side TTFT (we can use headless SDK runner to add client latency)
- Prepare an artifacts package and S3 transfer script (signed temporary credentials) 
- Run both hosted and a dedicated variant (if time) and capture p50/p90/p99 for TTFT and per-token latency
- Smoke test request error rates and KV cache hit rates (if applicable)

Schedule: run planned for 10/08–10/09. Please produce a short runbook and a timeline for the runs by EOD 10/07 so I can confirm with Liam.

Thanks — Olga

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneer.ai>, Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@pioneer.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-09T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pioneer MAP: performance scope & acceptance (latency/TTFT/concurrency) — results + next steps

Hi Liam / Sarah —

We completed the scheduled benchmarking runs (hosted Redwood API baseline + a dedicated config). High-level summary below; full CSVs and Grafana snapshots attached (pioneer-benchmark-results-20261008.csv + demo-ttft-screenshots.zip).

Summary (hosted baseline):
- Workload: corpus you supplied + synthetic steady-state to hit target QPS. Token distribution: short 61% / medium 31% / long 8% (close to plan).
- Steady-state: 120 QPS sustained (we also exercised your requested 350 QPS 30s spikes).
- TTFT (client-sim / measured at SDK runner): p50 = 95 ms, p90 = 180 ms, p99 = 245 ms -> PASS (acceptance threshold p99 <= 250 ms).
- First-token server egress: p50 = 80 ms, p90 = 160 ms, p99 = 210 ms.
- Per-token latency (subsequent tokens, medium prompts): p50 = 12 ms, p90 = 28 ms, p99 = 380 ms -> flagged: p99 higher than our target (350 ms) under sustained long token generation; appears correlated with cache misses for long-sequence paths.
- Error rate: 0.6% overall (within 2% threshold).
- Concurrency: achieved 350 concurrent inflight requests during spike window with graceful queueing/fallback; tail latency increases at >300 concurrent requests for long sequences.

Dedicated run: similar profile, slightly better tail per-token latencies (p99 ~ 330 ms) — likely due to increased KV cache locality.

Conclusion / recommended next steps:
1) MAP acceptance: Host baseline meets client-observed TTFT acceptance p99 <= 250 ms and error-rate criteria. Per-token p99 exceeded target in hosted baseline; dedicated config brings it under threshold.
2) Recommended follow-ups before final close: enable prefix KV caching for long sequences and retest the long-sequence p99 path (Neha can implement a cache tweak and rerun a targeted job).
3) Rollout plan: propose canary with 10% traffic on dedicated config for 48 hours, monitor TTFT and per-token p99. If canary meets p99 targets, proceed to full pilot.

Next actions and owners:
- Redwood (Neha): implement caching tweak + targeted rerun (ETA 10/12).
- Pioneer (Liam): confirm S3 bucket ACL for artifact transfer and sign-off on canary window (10/13–10/15 suggested).
- Joint: schedule a 30-min results walkthrough (I can do 10/12 10:00 PT).

If this meets your needs, please reply with sign-off on the MAP acceptance (hosted baseline meets TTFT acceptance; dedicated recommended for full per-token p99 compliance) and we'll schedule the canary run.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
